messages:
elaine: quick design idea — instead of the full-screen modal for creating API keys, what if we try a compact right-side panel that keeps users in context? thinking it could reduce cognitive jump when you create+use a key for a route. attaching mock in Figma.

 tom: +1 to keeping context. question about primary CTA — should it be Create (copy hidden) or Create & Reveal? usability wise people expect to see the secret once.

 maria: for implementation, side panel is easy, but we need a clear keyboard focus flow: panel opens, focus -> name input -> generated secret reveal button -> copy button. also need a path where users can skip reveal entirely.

 nick: accessibility nit: when a secret is revealed we must announce it to screen readers with aria-live politely (e.g., "API key revealed. Please copy now — this is your only time to see it"). avoid auto-selecting so AT users can opt to copy. also ensure the panel has role="dialog" and focus trap.

 tom: copy-wise propose: primary CTA = "Create and reveal" and secondary = "Create (hide secret)". but language must warn about single-view only. current empty states also silently imply you can see secrets later which is wrong.

 elaine: good point. suggestion for warning line under name field: "This key will only be shown once — make sure to copy it now or store it in a safe place." short and scannable.

 maria: implementation detail — when user chooses Create (hide) we'll show an ephemeral banner with a button to download the keyfile for 30s. backend can return a one-time token. API: 
```
POST /api-keys
body: { name, reveal: false }
returns: { id, oneTimeDownloadUrl? }
```

 nick: that one-time download URL needs an accessibility-friendly label for the link and a clear reachable focus target. also ensure link has rel="noopener" and times out server-side.

 tom: layout question: should the copy/download affordance live inside the panel after creation, or as a toast? I lean panel so people see it anchored to the object they created. toast can disappear too fast and is less discoverable for keyboard users.

 elaine: agree anchored panel. also propose an inline help icon next to the warning that opens a short explainer (one sentence + link to docs). keeps the copy concise while providing depth.

 maria: quick CSS/accessibility note — panel width ~420px looks good on 1366px width. when reduced to mobile we should fallback to full-screen modal. keyboard users on small screens still need focus trap.

 nick: a11y checklist: focus management, role=dialog, aria-labelledby to the panel title, aria-describedby to include the one-time message, visible focus indicators, and ensure copy button announces "copied to clipboard" with aria-live when used.

 elaine: empty state copy thought — current "No API keys yet" feels bland. propose: "No API keys yet — create one to get started. You’ll only see each key once." CTA: "Create API key". include a tiny help link under that says "How keys work".

 tom: microcopy tweak for revoke flow: when revoking we now show a contextual suggestion "If this key is in use by traffic-critical routes, rotate instead of revoke to avoid downtime". keep it subtle (muted text).

 maria: dev question: for rotate we need a dual-stage flow: create replacement key -> switch usages -> revoke old. UI should offer a checklist with 3 steps and a small progress indicator.

 nick: checklist must be keyboard navigable (checkboxes with proper labels) and should be announced to AT users when switching steps. also provide a skip/learn-more link.

 elaine: ok next actions: tom to update Figma with side panel and proposed CTAs, nick to draft the a11y checklist, maria to prototype keyboard flow and one-time download endpoint details, i'll write the microcopy variations and coordinate a small UX test with 5 devs.

 deploy-bot: figma update uploaded: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/compact-sidepanel — version: compact-panel-v2 (for review) :rocket:

 tom: cool — i'll iterate on the copy and drop updated strings here by EOD. anyone want to pair on the test script tomorrow?

 nick: i can pair morning, happy to run accessibility scenarios.

 maria: i'll stub API and share a small sandbox request for the team to try.

 elaine: thanks all — merging notes into the design doc and will ping product-ops for a quick usability session scheduling. :slightly_smiling_face:
